claims.text: As-processed refractory high-entropy alloys can exhibit very high strength.
As-processed refractory high-entropy alloys generally have limited ductility.
As-processed refractory high-entropy alloys deform nonuniformly under dynamic high-strain-rate conditions.
The proposed intervention is high-temperature deformation followed immediately by rapid quenching.
High-temperature deformation followed by rapid quenching will produce a metastable and spatially uniform microstructure in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The treatment will generate uniformly distributed nanoscale coherent precipitates.
The treatment will generate deformation twins that are retained by rapid quenching.
High-temperature deformation promotes controlled plastic flow.
High-temperature deformation promotes partial recrystallization.
Partial recrystallization initiates fine coherent structural features.
Rapid quenching freezes the deformation-produced uniform microstructure.
A metastable microstructure containing twins or related deformation features can combine enhanced ductility with high strength.
The treatment will improve ductility relative to untreated or conventionally processed refractory high-entropy alloys.
The treatment will make deformation more homogeneous relative to the untreated baseline.
The treated alloy will preserve high strength or incur only a minimal strength decrease.
The treatment will preserve dynamic impact-induced energy-release capability.
The expected benefits should hold under high-strain-rate impact from room temperature to moderately elevated temperatures.
Refractory high-entropy alloys can retain high strength over a broad range from room temperature to approximately 1073 K.
Above approximately 1073 K, diffusion-controlled deformation can soften refractory high-entropy alloys.
The optimal deformation temperature, strain, and quench rate remain undetermined.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires that energy-release performance not be sacrificed, whereas the falsification rule treats any alteration in energy-release behavior as falsifying; an improvement in energy release would therefore satisfy the hypothesis's objective but also trigger the stated falsification rule.
